title: snapshot.json — the engine's measured view of the city (engine → LLM, and a debugging artifact)
$comment: Mirrors Agora.Core.Contracts.CitySnapshot / DistrictSnapshot. Wire conventions for every Agora JSON file: property names are camelCase, SimDate is the string 'YYYY-MM-DD', and enums are their C# member names. Per-district numbers are best-effort (plan §6): a sensor that cannot resolve one copies the city value, sets hasCityFallbacks, and names the property in cityFallbackFields — so the dashboard never presents a city number as a local fact.

cityStatistics.$comment: What the game's own city statistics screen shows. CITY-ONLY, and not by omission: Game.Simulation.CityStatisticsSystem is keyed by (StatisticType, int parameter) and has no district dimension at all, so this block is deliberately absent from the district object rather than mirrored there as a permanent fallback. See docs/scout/0004-city-statistics.md §1.4.

homelessShare.$comment: 0-1. The game's CountHouseholdDataSystem.HomelessnessRate is a percentage 0-100; this is that number divided by 100, matching the fraction convention taxRates already uses. A threshold authored against the unconverted figure fires at 100x the intended homelessness.

movedAwayUnhappy.$comment: StatisticType.MovedAwayReason keyed by (int)MoveAwayReason.NotHappy. Separate from citizensMovedAway because 'nowhere to live' and 'miserable' are different political stories.

garbageProductionRate.$comment: Garbage PRODUCED per day, from GarbageAccumulationSystem.garbageAccumulation — the value the game's own binding names 'productionRate'. It is not a stockpile and does not fall when collection improves. Uncollected garbage is the separate uncollectedGarbage field, which is also the only garbage figure with a district breakdown.

tourismLevels.$comment: City-only. Game.City.Tourism exists on the city entity and nowhere else. Carries no landmark count: the game has no landmark concept — see signatureBuildingCount.

attractiveness.$comment: A dimensionless index, not a percentage, and stored raw rather than normalised because it is the exact quantity the shipped city-attractiveness effect moves.

progressionState.$comment: City-only by nature — a district has no level.

milestoneLevel.$comment: Game.City.MilestoneLevel.m_AchievedMilestone. This is ALSO 'city level': CS2 has no separate level counter, so the two names are one number.

resourceIndex.$comment: EconomyUtils.GetResourceIndex — the game's own small dense key, not the Resource flag value, which is a bitfield up to 1<<40 and sorts badly.

rate.$comment: A fraction, e.g. 0.10 for 10%. The game reports whole percentage points.

uncollectedGarbage.$comment: Summed Game.Buildings.GarbageProducer.m_Garbage. One of exactly three v4 fields that are genuinely per-district: the buildings behind them carry Game.Areas.CurrentDistrict. NOT the infoview's 'stored garbage', which comes from a private job — prose must say 'uncollected', never 'landfill'.

schemaVersion.$comment: v1 carried only population, happiness, unemployment and money. v2 is the M2 contract freeze. v3 adds the household budget: averageHouseholdUpkeep, averageHouseholdResourceSpend, averageHouseholdFees and the disposableMargin they add up to, city-wide and per district. v4 adds what the game's own city statistics screen exposes — statistics, tourism, progression, unlockedFeatureIds, industryTaxRates — plus the three counts that genuinely resolve per district. ADDITIVE ONLY: nothing was renamed or removed, and this document is not a sidecar so there is no migration to write; an old snapshot.json on disk is a debugging artifact, not state.

disposableMargin.$comment: Share of daily household income left after rent, upkeep, goods and utility fees. Signed and uncapped on purpose: negative means households are drawing down savings, which is the state the cost-of-living issue most needs to see.

signatureBuildingCount.$comment: What the rework plan called landmarkCount. There is no landmark concept anywhere in Game.dll — the only two occurrences of the word are DLC id lines — so the field is named for what is actually counted, the Game.Buildings.Signature tag.

unlockedFeatureIds.$comment: Unlocked feature PREFAB NAMES, sorted ordinal ascending. A feature carries no id of its own — Game.Prefabs.FeatureData is a zero-field tag — so the identity is the prefab and the portable id is PrefabSystem.GetPrefabName. There is no FeatureType enum and no hash. A list, so no metric-history series stands behind it and no delta trigger may name it.

industryTaxRates.$comment: Sorted by (area, resourceIndex) ascending. The order is contractual for the same reason districts' is. City-only: TaxSystem has no per-district, per-resource overload.

districts.$comment: Sorted by district id ascending. The order is contractual — the engine iterates this list, and an ECS-chunk-ordered list would make results depend on chunk layout.
